memories.content: The user's maternal aunt keeps one spare key to the user's home.
If the door is locked, the user is accustomed to contacting their maternal aunt, who has the spare key, before contacting building management.
When going to collect the spare key from their maternal aunt, the user wants to give an arrival time first so neither person has to wait.
The user feels at ease only after returning a borrowed spare key in person on the same day.
The user feels uneasy about writing down a new entrance passcode on paper.
The user found it difficult when a family member arrived without notice during a meeting and the user could not respond immediately.
On a day their younger brother received a package for them, the user felt reassured after checking the delivery photo.
The user's maternal aunt wants confirmation that the user is coming in person before handing over the spare key.
Confirm with the user before sharing the spare key's storage location or the maternal aunt's contact information.
The management office of a multi-unit residential building does not hold a unit key without verifying identity.
The user keeps basic repair tools in a box beneath the sink.
On a day the faucet leaked, the user placed only a towel beneath it, and the floor became wet as well.
After sending a photo to building management, the user finalized the time for a repair visit.
Before the technician's visit, the user emptied the area beneath the sink so work could begin immediately.
On a day the user wrote the visit time only in the calendar and turned off the reminder, they heard the doorbell late.
For the next visit, the user enabled a reminder 30 minutes beforehand and answered immediately at the entrance.
After the repair, the user called their maternal aunt to confirm that the spare key entrusted to her was still there.
The user's maternal aunt considers it unsafe to hand the spare key to a repair technician without the user's explicit request.
Obtain the user's reconfirmation before scheduling an external worker to enter the residential unit.
A multi-unit residential building's repair schedule may change because of emergency work or parts availability.

analysis.overview: Both frames support the aunt’s continuing custody of the spare key. They add context-specific practices for coordinating arrivals, responding promptly, and authorizing key release, while separately covering lockouts, privacy, deliveries, repairs, worker access, and building procedures without contradiction.
